status: Algorithm review only; no new kernel, deployment, device qualification or performance result
current_component: AIC computes paired gate/up tiles and publishes one private non-reused flag after FIX completion. GU and A are full canonical training saves.
Both AIV subcores participate in activation: subcore0 consumes rows0..63 and subcore1 rows64..127 for each128-row tile. No subcore is reserved for communication.
There is no activation-ready flag for in-kernel GMM2. The current Python adapter relies on whole UpSwiGLU kernel completion before grouped GMM2, then a separate gate and SHMEM combine.
The inherited P1 backward remains staged; this component is grouped W1 plus SwiGLU, not a fused communication/complete forward/backward pipeline.
next_integration_requirements: A candidate reserving AIV1 for communication must explicitly move the full actual128 rows of each pair to AIV0. Merely reassigning subcore1 would silently drop half the activation rows. Retain partial/tail/empty handling and existing BF16 cast sequence.

Add separate activation completion after the final MTE3 store visibility fence. AIC down consumers wait for the exact actual set of activation N tiles for their M tile; a GU-ready flag alone is insufficient.

For targetI2048, each128-row M tile has8 G/U pairs. A512-row wave has32 pairs/64 up GEMMs and96 down tiles. Assign all up work before any AIC waits on activation completion to avoid waiting for unscheduled up producers.

Implement a compute-only up/activation/down wave first as a distinct native candidate with full GU/A/Z saves, compared against the already-qualified staged arithmetic. This can verify new roles and intra-wave producer/consumer counts before changing SHMEM completion/reuse.

When communication is integrated, dispatch readiness must cover every actual source contribution to canonical Xe rows. Existing whole-operation completion must not be relabelled as per-wave completion without a real device publication point and visibility proof.
Maintain rounded unweighted BF16 Z through backward for zero-gate dp. Gate each contribution in FP32 then BF16 at the same boundary as the control, preserving deterministic source reduction.

Separate permanent saved-tensor allocation from transport staging. Adding full temporary return slots may exceed existing SHMEM half/workspace limits even when local saved tensors fit; derive actual remote slot/credit sizes from the transport ABI before allocation.

Use distinct producer-ready, local transport-complete and remote-consumed epochs for any reused staging slot. Communication progress must drain current returns before waiting for future dispatch credits that those returns release. No speculative removal of barriers, quiet or final handshake.

target_saved_tensors.scope: R65536,H6144,I2048 per rank, BF16, logical saved tensor storage; excludes weights, gradients, oracle, SHMEM and temporary buffers
target_saved_tensors.limit: Balanced65536 is not a skewed-route capacity bound; use actual counts and checked64-bit arithmetic.

comparison: Keep staged P0, P1 vector arithmetic, P2 same-order serial/overlap, P3 grouped-up component and new wave candidates separately identified. Compare source-compatible math/route/save costs and complete gradients before timing. Use comm-only/compute-only/forced serial/fused with identical actual chunk workload; hardware intervals and max-rank full-step timing establish the benefit. No sum of overlapping stages or empty-AIV source specialization proves physical overlap.
next_device_priority: Current authorized pending EP2 P2 overlap and reviewed EP16 progression retain priority. This review does not create a competing NPU job or authorize compilation/deployment of a new wave kernel.
